(Premise, prize, rule, and the emotional wound 'she broke up with me' all land inside 20s; handcuffs click on at 0:29.)
premise: Two exes (Suzie and Josh; dated 4 years, split 3 years ago, she dumped him) are handcuffed to a 60-ft chain in a sealed box for 30 days. Every ~5 days Jimmy returns with an offer that shortens the chain in exchange for money or a mystery door. At day 25 the format flips: either person can unhandcuff to steal the entire $250,000 + both Teslas, leaving the other with $0. It is a survival-challenge chassis carrying a rekindled-romance story with a prisoner's-dilemma finale.
stakes: $250,000 stated at 0:10 ("I will give them $250,000"). Loss condition at 0:31-0:36: cross the red line and "neither of you wins anything." Stakes escalate in steps: +$25K for a 30-ft chain (4:04); mystery door revealed as two $40K Teslas (19:18, 19:30); day-25 twist (23:49-24:14) converts shared stakes into zero-sum: "you actually get all $250,000 and both Teslas... and the other person gets $0." Emotional stakes run in parallel from 0:19 ("She broke up with me") and 17:05 (the secret Josh had to sell).

click_levers: TITLE GRAMMAR: imperative dare + number stack — "Survive [30 Days] [absurd constraint: Chained To Your Ex], Win [$250,000]". Second-person 'Your Ex' makes the viewer imagine themselves in it; two big numbers (duration + prize) promise scale. THUMBNAIL (read from the image): overhead shot of two people lying cheek-to-cheek on a white pillow; a thick silver chain wrapped around BOTH necks; the man (brown hair, beard, blue pajamas — the face reads as Jimmy himself, standing in for Josh, who does not appear on the thumb) grimaces with bared teeth and wide eyes; the woman (blonde, pink sleep mask, pink polka-dot pajamas) scowls sideways at him; handwritten "DAY 29" top-right. EXPECTATION VIOLATED: (1) exes forced into bed-level intimacy — repulsion + proximity in one frame; (2) the chain is around the neck (video uses wrist handcuffs), an exaggeration of the 1-ft chain that only arrives at 33:22, so the thumb sells the LAST state of the video and you must watch ~33 min to reach it; (3) 'DAY 29' implies 'they nearly made it and hate each other' — the video pays that off inversely with a reconciliation, kiss, and $125K each, i.e. the promised misery resolves as romance.

click_levers: TITLE GRAMMAR: [Imperative 'Survive'] + [duration '30 Days'] + [impossible constraint 'Trapped In The Sky'] + [comma] + [explicit reward 'Win $250,000'] — the MrBeast 'Survive X in Y, Win $Z' template: task, place, dollar figure, no ambiguity about what the video is. THUMBNAIL (read from ZFoNBxpXen4.jpg): MrBeast HIMSELF — not the two contestants — sits cross-legged on a bed-sized square metal platform with yellow/black hazard striping, wearing a torn, dirt-smeared red hoodie and sweatpants, socks with holes; on the platform: a grimy pillow, blue blanket, toilet-paper roll, two water bottles, dirty white sneakers; the platform floats above clouds with green farmland far below; a helicopter hovers at right. His face is exhausted/pleading, looking into camera. No text overlay. Torn clothes = time has passed; helicopter = no way down; domestic objects (pillow, TP) on a deadly ledge = the absurd premise in one frame. The thumb sells first-person identification (the viewer/Jimmy stranded), while the video is actually two strangers — Jimmy only hosts. EXPECTATION VIOLATED: (1) a human cannot 'live' on a floating square — the image collides survival-camping props with a lethal drop; (2) the title promises 'Survive... Win' but the hidden mechanics (floor shrinks every failure 04:46; partner leaving makes YOUR prize bigger 01:29; a bait-and-switch smaller beam 18:34; final offer to double to $500k 32:00) mean the real question becomes 'does anyone come down with money?' — Angus falls out at 19:30, so the title's promise is only half-kept.

THUMBNAIL (read from oBXSvS2QKxU.jpg): left third, MrBeast in a black-and-white referee shirt, eyes wide, mouth open in shock, looking at camera; center, a huge bald, bearded strongman in a torn red tracksuit, teeth gritted, being swarmed — children in matching blue tracksuits with white stripes cling to his neck, arms and legs and pull at his clothes so the fabric visibly rips; a sea of hundreds more kids fills the frame to the horizon on a green field. No text overlay. Red (strongman) vs blue (kids) color-codes the two teams, matching the video's red-marker/red-line rules at 22:54. The thumb depicts a physical pile-on/brawl, whereas the actual event is a rope tug-of-war — it dramatizes the outcome, not the mechanic. The referee framing casts Jimmy as neutral arbiter of an obviously absurd 'fair fight.' EXPECTATION VIOLATED: intuition says one man who pulls a 50,000-lb plane (09:05) drags 100 children; the thumbnail shows him overwhelmed, and the video pays off bigger — 100 kids beat all TEN strongmen (27:06). Secondary: the title sells one matchup but the video is a 7-segment anthology; the title fight is only the final ~5 minutes.

title: Last To Leave Grocery Store, Wins $250,000
hook_verbatim: 00:00 I just bought this grocery store, / 00:01 and I have a big surprise for everyone. / 00:04 Hey, MrBeast! / 00:05 Hey, everybody! / 00:08 YEAHHHHHHH! / 00:09 Attention, everybody… / 00:10 You are now in a MrBeast video. / 00:13 Whichever one of you leaves this grocery store last / 00:17 wins that $250,000 right there. / 00:20 This is gonna be interesting. / 00:21 I don't know any of these people. / 00:22 They're not my friends. They're just random shoppers. / 00:25 And I'm sure they have a lot of questions. / 00:26 Let's go talk to 'em. / 00:27 Do you know that you're in a MrBeast video right now? / 00:30 A mister what???
premise: MrBeast buys a real grocery store, runs a 50%-off sale to fill it with random shoppers (02:04), then announces over the PA that whoever leaves last wins $250,000. Contestants must live in the store using only what is inside (02:29), step on a red line and you are out (01:15), and 'this video can go as long as they want' (03:12). ~100 strangers (31:41) become factions, villains and fan favorites over 67 days, with the host returning periodically to escalate.
stakes: Prize: $250,000 cash physically shown ('wins that $250,000 right there', 00:13-00:17). Cost side stated immediately after: real jobs ('If I don't leave and go back to the job, I have no job after this', 00:44; 'She has to come to WORK!', 00:55), then kids/family (Juan sends his son home 13:01; Autumn 17:17; Robbie 'not gonna be in here for three months and miss my kid's life' 17:33). Consequence rule: red line = elimination (01:15). Stakes escalate: Square $5K + gift box per leaver (22:04-22:23), $50K leader-controlled bribe (30:30), $30K+$5K taken (31:10), windows boarded on Day 30 (26:49), store halved (33:06), and finally the $1M offer (41:12).

premise: Jimmy and four friends (Chandler, Nolan, Hase — the only one who's 'kinda built one' — and cameraman Darius) are dropped on a Pacific island and must scavenge bamboo and washed-up ship trash (four blue barrels become the MacGuffin) to build a barrel-catamaran sailboat, then paddle/sail 5+ miles across a channel with a deadly sideways current to a neighboring island. A deliberate throwback to the 'hanging out with the boys' era (12:21-12:47) — no contestants, no prize — and it ENDS IN FAILURE 0.5 miles short.

title: I Stranded 100 People In The Wilderness For $250,000
hook_verbatim: 00:00 "I just stranded these 100 people in the middle of the wilderness." 00:03 "And whichever team has the most people here" 00:05 "when help arrives, splits that two hundred fifty thousand dollars." 00:09 "The people wearing blue are a team of survival experts," 00:12 "and the people wearing red are amateurs" 00:14 "who might not be cut out for the wilderness." 00:17 "Blue Team, grab your bags and follow me." 00:19 "What's the longest you've spent in the woods?" 00:22 "Three months!" 00:22 "Like for fun?" 00:23 "Yeah!" 00:24 "Oh, my gosh." 00:25 "How many of you have been camping before?" 00:27 "Mmm..." 00:28 "How many of you could survive a month out here?" 00:30 "Oh, my gosh, they're COOKED over there." 00:32 "I knew the Blue Team would have an advantage." — Premise, prize, win condition AND the two-team asymmetry are all delivered by 0:16; the rest of the first 30s is contrast interviews that set the expected outcome (experts win) so the video can violate it.
premise: 50 survival experts (Blue) vs 50 amateurs (Red) are dropped in the same forest for ~20 days. The amateurs were told the challenge in advance and taken to a store (tents, tarps, 24-pack of water, lighters); the experts were only told 'MrBeast video' (0:34-0:57). Anyone can quit at any time by lighting a flare (2:03). Jimmy periodically injects mini-games (50-can temptation at 10:57, 5-box prisoner's dilemma at 21:55, hidden flare-gun hunt at 31:52). Whichever team has more members still in camp when the game ends splits $250,000. The framing question is skill vs resources; the delivered answer is teamwork (36:48).
stakes: $250,000 split among whichever team has the most people remaining, stated at 0:03-0:08 in the first sentence. Restated by contestant Randy at 6:24-6:32 ('The team with the most members left... will win and divide up the $250,000 prize'). Stakes ESCALATE per-person as people quit: 19:26-19:33 'It's good that more people are dropping... Ka-ching! Every time someone leaves the pot gets bigger'; 26:31-26:47 'their share of the $250,000, if they win, is going up... it's starting to become A LOT of money.' Consequence of losing is stated only at the end: losers get $4,000 each (36:39), winners walk home with $22,000 each (36:44). Secondary stakes: physical toll ('losing weight every day... until my body starts shutting down' 18:57-19:02) and the 'you still lose if you fire the flare while behind' bet at 32:19.
